summary: Submitted the fixed experiment for the restore-on-monotonic-store reachability question (d3822b1a6c4f4904b1115427ad452104-question-0): a real single-node cluster over the test monotonic log store with default TrailingLogs/SnapshotThreshold and SnapshotInterval shortened to 150ms, an internal snapshot opened with its index raised by 100, the production Restore run, and store last index / snapshot index / applied index / stored-snapshot count / shouldSnapshot sampled before the restore, straight after it, and after 700ms. Native construction feedback with those fixed inputs produced a negative result that constrains the earlier claim: after the restore store_last=105 while snapshot_index=104, so the store was not emptied and should_snapshot stayed false, with the stored-snapshot count unchanged after the interval - most likely because the Restore API appends a trailing noop that leaves one entry above the snapshot index. Recorded the experiment for controller execution; the measured interpretation and any narrowing of the asserted defect's limitations are left for the retained receipt.
